extracted.intended_audience: aspiring poets, literary critics, and students of poetic theory
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and evaluating poems and for recognising poetic genius—covers imagination vs. fancy, what constitutes a poem/poetry, suitable subjects, unity of parts, versification, imagery, and intellectual depth. Intended as practical-critical criteria for poets and critics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: “The primary Imagination I hold to be the living power and prime agent of all human perception, and as a repetition in the finite mind of the eternal act of creation in the infinite I AM.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as the originating creative faculty: the living power that underlies perception and creation. Emphasise originality, generative creativity, and the notion that poetic perception itself is an act akin to creation. Use this as the highest standard for poetic originative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary Imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: “The secondary Imagination I consider as an echo of the former, co-existing with the conscious will, yet still as identical with the primary in the kind of its agency, and differing only in degree, and in the mode of its operation. It dissolves, diffuses, dissipates, in order to recreate: or where this process is rendered impossible, yet still at all events it struggles to idealize and to unify.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative re-working rather than raw origination: evaluates the poet’s ability to dissolve and re-create images and material, to idealize and unify disparate elements under conscious control. Distinguish this from mere memory or association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fancy (vs Imagination)
rubrics_metrics.description: “FANCY, on the contrary, has no other counters to play with, but fixities and definites. The fancy is indeed no other than a mode of memory emancipated from the order of time and space... equally with the ordinary memory the Fancy must receive all its materials ready made from the law of association.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern for poetic invention: fancy is mechanical recombination of preexisting images drawn from association and memory. Use this criterion to penalize work that shows cleverness or ornament but lacks synthetic imaginative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Poem (immediate object: pleasure)
rubrics_metrics.description: “A poem is that species of composition, which is opposed to works of science, by proposing for its immediate object pleasure, not truth; and from all other species... it is discriminated by proposing to itself such delight from the whole, as is compatible with a distinct gratification from each component part.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: immediate aim should be pleasure (in the poetic sense) rather than demonstration of truth; the poem must provide delight both from the whole and from each component part. Evaluate whether parts justify metrical arrangement and contribute to cumulative pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of Parts / Mutual Support
rubrics_metrics.description: “A legitimate poem... the parts of which mutually support and explain each other; all in their proportion harmonizing with, and supporting the purpose and known influences of metrical arrangement.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key evaluative standard: parts must cohere and harmonize so each element contributes to the whole. Anti-patterns: a series of striking lines that stand alone, or an unsustained composition where the whole yields a general result but components fail to gratify individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader Engagement Dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: “The reader should be carried forward, not merely or chiefly by the mechanical impulse of curiosity, or by a restless desire to arrive at the final solution; but by the pleasurable activity of mind excited by the attractions of the journey itself.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the poem engages the reader through continuous pleasurable attention rather than mere plot-curiosity or gimmickry. Reward work that makes the ‘journey’ itself rewarding and varied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry beyond Metre (poetry in prose)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The writings of Plato... furnish undeniable proofs that poetry of the highest kind may exist without metre... poetry... excites a more continuous and equal attention than the language of prose aims at, whether colloquial or written.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not equate poetry solely with metre/rhyme. Evaluate on capacity to sustain continuous, heightened attention and imaginative intensity; formal metre is neither necessary nor sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Studied Selection and Artificial Arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: “The remaining parts must be preserved in keeping with the poetry; and this can be no otherwise effected than by such a studied selection and artificial arrangement...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the poet’s editorial judgment and arrangement skills—selection and ordering should maintain poetic quality and attention. Penalise careless composition that fails to shape material into a single harmonious effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two Classes of Subjects (Lyrical Ballads plan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan that poems may be of two sorts: (1) incidents and agents supernatural or romantic, aiming to interest affections by dramatic truth; (2) subjects from ordinary life whose novelty is produced by awakening attention to the familiar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing subjects, evaluate whether the poet achieves the intended effect: for supernatural/romantic pieces, does the work secure believable emotional truth and willing suspension of disbelief? For ordinary-life pieces, does it awaken attention and reveal novelty in the familiar?

rubrics_metrics.name: Language Appropriate to Subject (language of ordinary life)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wordsworth proposed to manage certain subjects “in the language of ordinary life” to produce pleasurable interest; Coleridge warns against doctrinaire extension of this rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: the diction must suit the subject and purpose. Avoid dogmatic application of 'language of real life' where richer or more artificial diction better serves unity and effect. Penalise mismatches between style and subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical Sweetness of Versification
rubrics_metrics.description: “The perfect sweetness of the versification; its adaptation to the subject; and the power displayed in varying the march of the words without passing into a loftier and more majestic rhythm than was demanded by the thoughts...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical mastery of versification: musicality, appropriateness to subject, and variety within restraint. Distinguish original musical sensibility from mechanical, imitable metrics; originality in sound is highly prized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Subjects Remote from Private Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: “A second promise of genius is the choice of subjects very remote from the private interests and circumstances of the writer himself... where the subject is taken immediately from the author’s personal sensations and experiences, the excellence... is but an equivocal mark.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer imaginative reach over autobiographical immediacy as a sign of maturity/genuineness. Treat intensely personal material with caution—commend it only when it demonstrates imaginative transformation rather than mere reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery Modified by Predominant Passion / Reduction to Unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Images become proofs of original genius only as far as they are modified by a predominant passion; or by associated thoughts or images awakened by that passion; or when they have the effect of reducing multitude to unity, or succession to an instant; or lastly, when a human and intellectual life is transferred to them from the poet’s own spirit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether imagery is integrated with a controlling emotion or idea (predominant thought), whether it unifies complex material, creates simultaneity from succession, and imbues images with intellectual/personified life. Penalise decorative imagery that lacks this synthetic function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery Suited to Circumstances and Character
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagery is of higher worth when it 'moulds and colours itself to the circumstances, passion, or character, present and foremost in the mind.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate fit: images should arise naturally from dramatic/personal circumstances and character, not be generic ornaments. Reward images that reveal character and situation through apt metaphor and tonal alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth and Energy of Thought
rubrics_metrics.description: “No man was ever yet a great poet, without being at the same time a profound philosopher. For poetry is the blossom and the fragrancy of all human knowledge, human thoughts, human passions, emotions, language.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: intellectual depth and serious thought underpin great poetry. Reward works that combine imaginative power with philosophical/reflective energy; penalise lightweight pieces that show surface charm but lack substantive thought.
